newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Tietmeyer says G10 sees signs of growth in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says G10 sees signs of growth in Japan.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said there were signs of strong growth in Japan's real economy.

But Tietmeyer, speaking after a meeting of G10 central bank governors, said the bankers believed that most economies in continental Europe were still in a period of structural adjustment. Tietmeyer said the G10 central bank governors had however singled out the Netherlands as having an improving economy.
"As far as Japan is concerned, first of all there are now in the real economy signs of strong growth," Tietmeyer said.
Tietmeyer said recent gross domestic product data for the first quarter in Japan had been "relatively strong," and the latest Tankan survey showed increasing confidence.
"Of course, one has to wait and see what will be the future developments," Tietmeyer said, regarding Japan.
Tietmeyer said the G10 central bankers also had a brief discussion about the economic situation in Europe.
"On the one hand the situation in the Netherlands is improving, as you know," Tietmeyer said.
"On the other hand, most countries in continental Europe are in a structural adjustment process," Tietmeyer added, without specifying which countries he was refering to.
"For the time being, monetary policy has not to play a special additional or changing role in those countries," he said.

Tietmeyer has in the past repeatedly said that central banks have done their share to revive continental European economies, and that it was now up to the governments to contribute to growth through measures like labour market liberalisation. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
